title: Governed architecture hotspot and responsibility boundaries
decision: Every discovered hotspot is either decomposed into an explicit responsibility unit or retained as a named bounded exception with no hidden persistence or transaction ownership.

surfaces.purpose: Owns the abnormality types screen user workflow and its tightly coupled loading, error, empty, and interaction states.
surfaces.authorityBoundary: Role and command admission is obtained from approved-user and feature providers before privileged actions; the screen does not own persistence.
surfaces.persistenceOwnership: No direct persistence is admitted; repositories, command services, or read providers own data access.
surfaces.transactionOwnership: No cross-source or database transaction is owned by this presentation surface.
surfaces.rationale: The file represents one cohesive operational screen or companion section whose state and widgets share one lifecycle; extraction beyond existing parts would split invariant UI state without reducing authority or persistence ownership.
surfaces.reArmCondition: Re-arm when the line ceiling is exceeded, observed responsibilities change, a required boundary marker disappears, a forbidden responsibility returns, or the named regression no longer passes.

surfaces.purpose: Owns the live morning-review workspace, frozen record view, ordered agenda, attendance, contribution, action and finalization presentation as one route.
surfaces.authorityBoundary: Approved-user, facilitator and role capabilities determine visible commands; the callable backend independently revalidates every mutation and the screen grants no authority from record payloads.
surfaces.persistenceOwnership: No direct persistence is admitted; actor-scoped read providers own Firestore reads and the exact command service owns callable transport.
surfaces.transactionOwnership: No client database or cross-source transaction is owned by this presentation surface; server command handlers own meeting mutations atomically.
surfaces.rationale: The live workspace and frozen record share one agenda vocabulary and interaction state while editors are already extracted; retaining them together keeps session refresh, facilitator controls and archive navigation coherent without mixing persistence into presentation.
surfaces.reArmCondition: Re-arm when the line ceiling is exceeded, responsibilities change, callable admission bypasses actor capability, direct persistence appears, or any named Morning Review regression fails.

surfaces.purpose: Owns the operational-event list, filtering, creation, update, resolution, recurrence and asset-scope workflow as one cohesive screen.

surfaces.persistenceOwnership: No direct persistence is admitted; the operational-event service and actor-scoped read providers own remote access.
surfaces.transactionOwnership: No cross-source or database transaction is owned by this presentation surface.
surfaces.rationale: Event occurrence state, asset scope, command dialogs and open/recent presentation share one lifecycle; further extraction would split the interaction invariant without reducing persistence ownership.
surfaces.reArmCondition: Re-arm when the line ceiling is exceeded, observed responsibilities change, actor-scoped admission disappears, a forbidden responsibility returns, or the named regression no longer passes.

surfaces.reArmCondition: Re-arm when the line ceiling is exceeded, responsibilities change, direct persistence appears, or inspection model regressions no longer pass.

surfaces.purpose: Owns the role-scoped inspection workspace, campaign coverage, findings, missing-target, and governed action presentation.
surfaces.authorityBoundary: Uses approved-user capabilities for affordances and sends mutations only through the governed workflow command boundary.
surfaces.persistenceOwnership: Read providers and the inspection repository own Firestore access; the screen owns none.
surfaces.transactionOwnership: Server command handlers own all inspection mutation transactions.
surfaces.rationale: The workspace is decomposed into editor and screen part files while preserving one route-level state and private visual language.
surfaces.reArmCondition: Re-arm when the line ceiling is exceeded, responsibilities change, command admission bypasses actor capability, or direct persistence appears.

surfaces.purpose: Owns closed-issue history, reopen admission, governed relevance retirement, and classification of qualifying resolved maintenance work.
surfaces.authorityBoundary: Approved-user capabilities control reopen and classification affordances; the backend revalidates issue finality, reopen-window expiry, asset identity, class version, and actor authority.
surfaces.persistenceOwnership: Maintenance and maintenance-intelligence providers own reads; mutations use governed workflow commands and this screen owns no direct database access.
surfaces.transactionOwnership: No client transaction is owned by the closed-ticket screen; server command handlers atomically own classification and cadence updates.
surfaces.rationale: The route coordinates one closed-issue dossier and its two history actions; optional metadata decoding is display-only and cannot grant mutation authority.
surfaces.reArmCondition: Re-arm when the line ceiling is exceeded, responsibilities change, decoded metadata becomes mutation authority, direct persistence appears, or classification bypasses the governed command boundary.

surfaces.purpose: Owns frequent-issue catalogue browsing and governed definition-management interactions.
surfaces.authorityBoundary: Uses approved-user catalogue capabilities and delegates mutations to the governed workflow command service.
surfaces.persistenceOwnership: The frequent-issue repository owns reads and the backend command owns writes.
surfaces.transactionOwnership: No client transaction is owned by the catalogue screen.
surfaces.rationale: The screen keeps one cohesive catalogue-management interaction while business parsing and persistence remain outside presentation.
surfaces.reArmCondition: Re-arm when the line ceiling is exceeded, responsibilities change, catalogue writes bypass the command boundary, or direct persistence appears.

surfaces.purpose: Owns maintenance-class, cadence, due-state, and planning workspace interactions.
surfaces.authorityBoundary: Uses approved-user planning capabilities and sends mutations only through governed workflow commands.
surfaces.persistenceOwnership: Read repositories and server command handlers own persistence; form serialization is limited to command payload construction.
surfaces.transactionOwnership: All maintenance-intelligence transactions remain server-owned.
surfaces.rationale: One workspace coordinates tightly related class definitions, live due state, and planning decisions without owning persistence.
surfaces.reArmCondition: Re-arm when the line ceiling is exceeded, responsibilities change, direct persistence appears, or a planning mutation bypasses the command boundary.

surfaces.purpose: Owns the governed planned-job dossier, module and diary affordances, maintenance classification display, and completion navigation.
surfaces.authorityBoundary: Approved-user capabilities control affordances; governed services and screens own all mutations, while metadata parsing is display-only.
surfaces.persistenceOwnership: Job, module, diary, and maintenance-intelligence providers own reads; this screen owns no direct database access.
surfaces.transactionOwnership: No database transaction is owned by the dossier.
surfaces.rationale: The route coordinates a single job dossier and delegates large visual sections to existing dossier parts while preserving one lifecycle.
surfaces.reArmCondition: Re-arm when the line ceiling is exceeded, responsibilities change, metadata becomes authority, or direct persistence appears.
